source.title: Dissociating Frontal Lobe Lesion Induced Deficits in Rule Value Learning Using Reinforcement Learning Models and a WCST Analog

confidence_rationale: The strongest falsifier-shaped evidence in this pull: five bilateral frontal lesion groups in 18 macaques on a WCST analog, with a reinforcement-learning model separating WHICH latent rule-learning parameter each lesion damaged. The deficits are qualitatively distinct rather than graded severities of one impairment, which is exactly the dissociable-signature pattern ARC-113's stage ablation predicts. Held below source_quality because per-group n is 3-4 and because the lesioned components correspond to only about three of ARC-113's eleven stages, so the ordered-cycle reading itself is untested here.
failure_signatures: Two of the five lesion groups (superior dorsolateral PFC, frontopolar cortex) produced NO significant deficit on any learning-rate parameter and no impairment on overall WCST performance, so a naive one-region-per-stage reading of the rule pipeline is refuted by this dataset.

ACC, PS and OFC groups all showed REDUCED model fit after lesion, which the authors attribute to task-related factors their RL model does not capture; a stage decomposition read only through fitted parameters can therefore miss real post-ablation structure.

OFC and ACC lesions BOTH increased choice stochasticity (beta) and both impaired repeat-after-surprising-reward, so the dissociation is partial: some post-ablation signatures are shared across components rather than unique to one.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Orbitofrontal cortex lesions impaired rule value learning from both positive and negative feedback; principal sulcus lesion deficits were consistent with impoverished maintenance of rule representations in working memory; anterior cingulate cortex lesion impairments likely reflected inability to flexibly switch between trial-and-error and working-memory response modes.
mapping.ree_translation: Damaging different components of a rule-learning system produces qualitatively DIFFERENT failure signatures, not a common decrement. In ARC-113 terms this is direct support for stage non-collapsibility across three adjacent stages: representation (PS / working-memory maintenance of the rule), outcome comparison and regularity refinement (OFC / rule-value updating from feedback), and control of transitions between apprehension and application modes (ACC). If these stages were one reasoning module, all three lesions would degrade the same parameter.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a macaque colour/shape WCST analog with a low-dimensional, externally-cued rule space; ARC-113 concerns an eleven-stage cycle including counterfactual simulation, generalisation and long-term integration, none of which this task exercises. The paper establishes LOCAL dissociability among about three stages, not the ordered cycle. Aspiration lesions carry acknowledged white-matter damage, so region-to-stage attribution is weaker than the parameter-level dissociation itself. Anatomical dissociation in a primate brain is also a different evidence type from ARC-113's falsifier, which is a stage ablation inside the REE substrate.
mapping.source_context: 18 macaques (7 M. mulatta, 11 M. fuscata) across 5 bilateral lesion groups; computerised WCST analog, 300 trials/session, covert colour or shape rule inferred from binary feedback; last 10 pre-lesion vs first 10 post-lesion sessions.

confidence_components.notes: Within-subject pre/post design plus an explicit generative model raise source quality well above a correlational imaging study. Mapping fidelity is capped by partial stage coverage; transfer risk is moderate because the rule space is far simpler than REE's.
